name: One model version
description: One row, one `body` column, built by Postgres. `trial` is soma-gaps 2.4: a version sits in `verified` while its trial match is queued or being played, and without this the Submit screen would show a submission that had simply stopped moving. It carries the trial's own status and when it was queued, so the wait can be stated rather than guessed at. `provisional` is now sigma against the settled threshold from [vars] -- the same number pair's demand view calls settled -- rather than a hardcoded matches_played < 20 that could disagree with it.

input.query: SELECT json_build_object( 'id', m.id, 'owner', u.handle, 'game', g.slug, 'version', m.version, 'repo', m.repo, 'release_tag', m.release_tag, 'commit_sha', m.commit_sha, 'class', m.weight_class, 'size_bytes', m.size_bytes, 'param_count', m.param_count, 'status', m.status, 'reject_reason', m.reject_reason, 'created_at', m.created_at, 'trial', (SELECT json_build_object('match_id', t.id, 'status', t.status, 'preset', t.preset, 'queued_at', t.created_at) FROM matches t WHERE t.trial_model_id = m.id ORDER BY t.created_at DESC LIMIT 1), 'ratings', coalesce((SELECT json_object_agg(r.ladder, json_build_object( 'rating', r.conservative, 'mu', r.mu, 'sigma', r.sigma, 'provisional', r.sigma > ($2)::float8, 'matches', r.matches_played)) FROM ratings r WHERE r.model_id = m.id), '{}'::json)) AS body FROM models m JOIN users u ON u.id = m.owner_id JOIN games g ON g.id = m.game_id WHERE m.id = ($1)::uuid
